scopeNotes: New text needs independent review; earlier hashes do not certify it.
Map endpoints are not historical founding or extinction dates.

The imported Andoa destination covers 1492 to 1500 in the Pastaza border region. The account uses explicitly dated later evidence and does not claim that modern organizational forms, practices or boundaries were documented in 1492. Geometry is unchanged and unverified.

Andwa identity is not reduced to speaking Katsakati. Kichwa-speaking Andwa people remain Andwa, and the multiethnic settlements called Andoas are not treated as a single homogeneous ethnic population.

NAPE’s document is the Plan de Vida 2010 to 2020. The 2021 URL upload date is not a new plan date. Described institutions and livelihoods are attributed to that plan; proposals are not converted into achieved outcomes.

The plan gives the 2008 binational meeting as September 20 to 24, whereas Gómez Rendón and Salazar give May 2008. The card uses only the consistent year. Recognition descriptions vary between legal personality in 2003 and later federation/registration steps; no exact legal instrument is invented.
Gómez Rendón and Salazar’s own 2015 account describes four workshops, while Rosado’s later summary says five. The card avoids an aggregate count and uses the documented December 2013 event.

The 2015 linguistic article distinguishes partial memory, language attrition and recording limitations. It reports learning of Hipólito Arahuanaza’s death in 2012; the card does not claim independent demographic verification that no other speaker existed anywhere.
Rosado’s interview names are pseudonyms. They are not used as real biographical identities. Her analysis of authenticity disputes is not adopted as a judgment against Andwa self-identification.

The university report is by project participants and identifies the Dagua family potters as Andwa. It does not support treating every Canelos resident as Andwa. Its documentary is described from the written account and has not been independently watched.

The dictionary launch in February 2023 is distinct from the 2022 publication date mentioned by Rosado. The actual dictionary contents were not inspected, so no entry count or lexical reconstruction is presented as independently verified.
No archaeological first invention, population collapse statistic, present-day environmental certification or successor state is manufactured. Cultural continuity is explicit.
Independent historical review, identity and border verification, and depth certification remain pending.
